issues.description: Field 'name' of class Ride: the UML in problem_statement.md declares the attribute as private (-name: String) (problem_statement.md lines 21-24), but the solution implementation declares it as public (solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/Ride.java line 5: 'public String name;'). This visibility mismatch contradicts the UML and the exercise requirement to add public getters for attributes; leaving the field public can confuse students about the intended encapsulation and may cause tests or grading checks that expect a private field with a public getter to fail or produce inconsistent feedback.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the 'name' attribute private in Ride (change 'public String name;' to 'private String name;') in both the template and solution implementation, keep the public getter getName(), and ensure the constructor assigns the value to the private field. Update the template files to match the UML-declared visibility so students implement against the intended specification.
